title: Universal first-order thickenings and conormal sheaves for algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A first-order thickening of spaces means a representable closed immersion, tested on scheme charts [def-weil-closed-immersion], whose quasi-coherent ideal has square zero. A map $h:Z\to X$ is formally unramified if, for every first-order thickening $T\hookrightarrow T'$ of schemes over $X$, restriction $\operatorname{Hom}_X(T',Z)\to\operatorname{Hom}_X(T,Z)$ is injective. Every unramified map of spaces (unramified on etale scheme charts [def-weil-unramified-morphism]) is formally unramified. For every formally unramified $h$ there exist a first-order thickening $k:Z\hookrightarrow W_h$ and $h^+:W_h\to X$ with $h^+k=h$, such that every $X$-map $a:T\to Z$ from a first-order thickening $T\hookrightarrow T'$ over $X$ extends uniquely to an $X$-map $a^+:T'\to W_h$ with $a^+|_T=ka$. This property also holds for algebraic-space tests $T,T'$. On the common small etale topos of $Z$ and $W_h$, the ideal $\mathcal I_h=\ker(\mathcal O_{W_h}\to\mathcal O_Z)$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; write $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I_h$. If $h$ is a closed immersion with ideal $\mathcal K$, then $W_h$ is the closed subspace defined by $\mathcal K^2$, and this identification identifies $\mathcal C_{Z/X}$ with $\mathcal K/\mathcal K^2$. These identifications respect the canonical maps of ideals induced by maps of the corresponding thickenings.

proof.text: Choose compatible surjective etale scheme charts $V\to Z$, $U\to X$ by the chart criterion. If $h$ is unramified, $V\to U$ is unramified by the meaning of chartwise unramifiedness, hence formally unramified by the scheme lemma. The reverse implication of the chart criterion proves formal unramifiedness of $h$. Conversely, when $h$ is formally unramified the forward implication gives formal unramifiedness of every scheme map $V\to U$ in such a square.

For later use, universality against schemes implies universality against spaces: cover a test $T'$ by etale scheme charts and take their reductions over $T$. Base change of the defining square-zero ideal remains square zero by the ideal correspondence. Scheme-test lifts agree on overlaps, after an etale scheme cover of each overlap, by uniqueness. Since the target space is an fppf sheaf, these compatible maps glue uniquely. The same argument extends affine-test uniqueness or existence to nonaffine tests, using affine open covers of the charts.

Fix compatible surjective charts $V\to Z$, $U\to X$. The scheme existence theorem gives a universal thickening $V\hookrightarrow V^+$ over $U$; step 2 permits space tests. It is universal over $X$ as well: for an affine test $T\hookrightarrow T'$ and $T\to V$, the induced $T\to U$ lifts uniquely over $X$ as follows. The pullback $E=T'\times_XU$ is a scheme etale over $T'$ by representable etaleness. The given $T\to U$ gives a section $T\to E$ over $T'$. The scheme flat-unramified lifting lemma, applied to $E\to T'$, gives its unique lift $T'\to E$, equivalently the desired lift $T'\to U$; then universality over $U$ supplies the unique map to $V^+$. For uniqueness, any proposed map to $V^+$ induces this same lift to $U$. Apply step 2 again. For $R=V\times_ZV$, etale permanence makes $R\to Z$ etale, and the map $R\to U$ through either projection is formally unramified by the chart criterion. Thus the same construction gives a scheme $R^+$ universal over $X$. Lift both projections to $s^+,t^+:R^+\to V^+$ by universality of $V^+$. Etale transport says both are etale, and both squares with $R\hookrightarrow R^+$ and $V\hookrightarrow V^+$ are cartesian.

source.place: Tag 0606 (lemma-universal-thickening), first two paragraphs, using Tags 0604 and 0605(1).

proof.text: The atlas presentation identifies $R\rightrightarrows V$ with the kernel-pair relation of $V\to Z$. Lift its identity $V\to R$ to $V^+\to R^+$, and its inverse $R\to R$ to $R^+\to R^+$ using universality of $R^+$. Put $D^+=R^+\times_{t^+,V^+,s^+}R^+$. Since both projection squares in step 3 are cartesian, the inverse image of $V$ under the common middle-point map $D^+\to V^+$ is $D=R\times_{t,V,s}R$. Hence $D\hookrightarrow D^+$ is first order by the ideal pullback criterion. Lift composition $D\to R$ to $D^+\to R^+$. Each required equation for the endpoints follows from uniqueness for maps to $V^+$: its two sides restrict to the same endpoint map on the reduced test thickening. Every map from a field spectrum to $V^+$ or $R^+$ factors uniquely through $V$ or $R$, because a field has no nonzero square-zero elements. Thus the relation on algebraically closed field points is precisely that of $R\rightrightarrows V$. The geometric-point criterion, with base $S$, now proves that $(s^+,t^+)$ is a monomorphism and an equivalence relation on all scheme tests.

source.place: Tag 0606, paragraph constructing the etale equivalence relation; groupoids.tex Tag 0DT7 (lemma-etale-equivalence-relation).

proof.text: Take the algebraic-space quotient $W=V^+/R^+$, whose atlas $q:V^+\to W$ is etale surjective and whose kernel pair is $R^+$. The $X$-maps on $V^+$ agree along $s^+,t^+$ by their construction, so the quotient property gives $W\to X$. Likewise $V\to V^+\to W$ descends through $Z=V/R$ to $k:Z\to W$. This is a monomorphism: locally lift two sections of $Z$ to $V$; equality in $W$ is a section of $R^+$ joining their lifts, which lies in $R$ by the cartesian $s^+$ square. The two sections therefore agree in $Z$. Moreover $Z\times_WV^+=V$ as sheaves. Indeed etale locally a section of this pullback is represented by $v\in V$ and an arrow in $R^+$ from $v$ to a section of $V^+$. The cartesian $s^+$ square puts that arrow in $R$ and its other endpoint in $V$; the converse inclusion and uniqueness follow from monicity. Closed-immersion atlas locality therefore makes $k$ a representable closed immersion. Its ideal is square zero because its restriction to the covering $V^+\to W$ is the ideal of $V\hookrightarrow V^+$ (ideal correspondence). Hence $k$ is first order, and etale descent of universality applied to this cartesian atlas square proves it universal over $X$.

source.place: Tag 0606, last paragraph: quotient and descent; Tags 0605(2), 03MB (lemma-closed-immersion-ideals).

proof.text: On every scheme base change, the square-zero closed immersion $k:Z\hookrightarrow W$ is integral, universally injective and surjective: affine-locally it is a quotient by a square-zero ideal, and primes correspond bijectively because they contain that ideal. The integral-radicial invariance theorem therefore identifies the categories of etale algebraic spaces over $Z$ and $W$. This equivalence preserves coverings: etale families cover if and only if their pullbacks cover, since the base map is surjective on field-valued points (nilpotents vanish in fields). The enlarged-site comparison identifies sheaves on these sites with sheaves on the small etale scheme sites. Thus $Z$ and $W$ have the common small etale topos claimed, without asserting that every lifted etale space is a scheme. The closed-immersion module theorem makes $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_W\to k_*\mathcal O_Z)$ quasi-coherent over $\mathcal O_W$. Since $\mathcal I^2=0$, its action factors through $\mathcal O_Z$; the same theorem's essential-image assertion makes it quasi-coherent over $\mathcal O_Z$. Under the common topos this is exactly the claimed $\mathcal C_{Z/X}$.

source.place: Tag 05ZH (theorem-topological-invariance), the small/enlarged etale-site comparison of spaces-properties.tex 03G1, and 0607 (definition-universal-thickening).

proof.text: Suppose $h:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is closed with ideal $\mathcal K$. Form the closed subspace $X_1=V(\mathcal K^2)$ by the ideal correspondence. The ideal $\mathcal K^2$ is quasi-coherent: on each affine etale chart it is the module of finite sums of products of elements of the ideal, and these products localize, giving compatible local module presentations. The induced $Z\hookrightarrow X_1$ has square-zero ideal $\mathcal K/\mathcal K^2$. Given a test thickening with ideal $\mathcal J$ and $b:T'\to X$ restricting through $Z$, the factorization criterion gives $b^\sharp(\mathcal K)\subseteq\mathcal J$. Thus $b^\sharp(\mathcal K^2)\subseteq\mathcal J^2=0$, and $b$ factors uniquely through $X_1$. Its restriction is the prescribed map to $Z$, since $Z\to X$ is a monomorphism. This proves universality directly. Comparing the two universal thickenings on their identity maps of $Z$ gives inverse maps $W\simeq X_1$: both composites are identities by uniqueness. Their ring-sheaf maps identify the kernels, so $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal K/\mathcal K^2$.

For a map of thickenings, the ring-sheaf map sends each kernel into the other kernel: a section killed by the structure quotient still maps to zero after the commuting quotient square. Under $W\simeq V(\mathcal K^2)$ this sends a class $a\bmod\mathcal K^2$ to the class of its ring-map image modulo the target ideal squared. This is exactly the induced map of ideals. The square-zero description uses the identical kernel map. Thus the identifications preserve all the canonical ideal maps asserted in the statement; no arbitrary choice of a module isomorphism enters.
